results.title: How a trade war could move American EVs out of reach - E&E News by POLITICO
results.content:
Hyundai officially opened its huge new EV factory in Georgia last month. Last week, the startup Sila began commissioning its first factory in Washington state to make silicon anodes, a new kind of battery component where China has no advantage. And Lyten, a maker of lithium-sulfur batteries, said it had bootstrapped enough domestic supplies to have a “tariff-free battery.” [...] The tariffs are threatening to raise the costs of minerals used to build equipment like lithium-ion batteries and other equipment coming into the U.S. The materials from China that matter most are battery cells; cathode-active materials; and raw inputs like graphite, lithium, cobalt and nickel. [...] Advertisement

Among the sufferers are new members of the American battery supply chain. Even as they make tariff-free materials domestically, they rely on equipment and chemicals from China, South Korea and Europe. Deals are on hold as everyone waits for clarity on presidential tariff decrees that shift by the day and week.

results.title: Tariff Resources and Strategies | GaMEP at Georgia Tech
results.content:
Reshoring: Consider automation opportunities and domestic suppliers (including those who can expand their production).
 Nearshoring: Take advantage of duty-free imports through Mexico.
 Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States Chapter 98 and Chapter 99: Eliminate or reduce duties for qualifying products.
 Bonded warehouses: Store imported products while deferring duties until they leave the facility (quarterly harbor maintenance fees apply). [...] As global trade evolves, manufacturers — either directly or indirectly — may face new challenges, such as adjusting pricing strategies, disrupting supply chains, and rising production expenses.

However, you can manage your risk and reduce your tariff burden through expert guidance and strategic solutions:

## Alternative Tariff Strategies [...] Foreign trade zones: Manufacture domestically while deferring or reducing duties based on the final product classification.
 First sale rule: Pay duties based on the manufacturer or middleman price (rather than the importer price).

## Tariff Resources

 Harmonized Tariff Schedule: View exempt products (updated regularly).
 U.S. Customs and Border Protection Centers of Excellence and Expertise (industry-specific):
  + Ask questions, such as how tariffs apply to specific industries.
